title: The frontend labels the identifier fields 'Passport number' and 'Ear tag number' with worked examples beneath; DR1 labels them 'Passport' and 'Ear tag'.

finding.frontend: A person entering a cow's details reads 'Passport number' over the first box and 'Ear tag number' over the third, each with an example underneath — 'For example, UK123456789' and 'For example, UK123456789012'. The labels and hints are authored in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/copy/copy.en.js:58-72.
finding.prototype: DR1 labels the same two boxes 'Passport' and 'Ear tag' — the identifier's name and nothing more. The labels come straight from the identifier data at app/data/commodity-identifiers.js:9-12 and are rendered as the govukInput label at app/views/animal-identification-details.html:111-120.
finding.difference: Change the two labels in the identification copy block to 'Passport' and 'Ear tag' so they read the same as the identifier names used everywhere else in the service, including the entered-records list and the check-answers card, which today already say 'Passport' and 'Ear tag' from a second label set in the same file. That second set exists only because the two do not agree; unifying them removes it. The finding is about the labels alone — DR1 sets no hint on any identifier field, but leaving the worked examples in place is a separate decision.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding 'Passport number' or 'Ear tag number' as the label text on DR1's identification panel for any commodity.
finding.correction: Sound, and observed on both sides in the screenshots and in both page models. Three notes. The scope is right: of the identifiers the two sides share, only these two labels differ — 'Tattoo' and 'Horse name' read the same word for word on both. The claim about the second label set holds too: the frontend really does carry two vocabularies for the same six identifiers in one file, the entry labels at commodities/copy/copy.en.js:58-79 and the summary labels at :48-55, and the second set is what the entered-records list and the check-answers identifier table both read (check-answers/view-model/cards/consignment/species/identifier-columns.js:9-16). The title is the weak part: it leads with the worked examples, which the finding then rules out of scope in its last sentence, so a reader scanning titles will expect the hints to go and they will not. Leaving them is the right call — DR1 sets no hint on any live-animal identifier, but the frontend's are additive help rather than a contradiction of DR1, and deleting help is poor work to schedule. This is the one place that decision is recorded, so it should stay recorded here.
